result:
The board push gate is built and PR #408 is out of draft. The jobs selftest passed (1827 checks, 0 failures) and preflight passed. CI on the new head (`47b6cd26bb`) is still running; nothing else is pending from this lane.

**Why attempt 1 didn't finish:** it opened the draft PR, pushed a stub `NOTES.md`, and ended. Nothing else had been built, and it wasn't waiting on anything. This is now recorded in `docs/lanes/boardpushgate/NOTES.md`.

**What's in the PR:**
- **`jobs/board-push-gate.sh`** runs `check_territory.py` and `check_coverage.py` against a candidate board, using a throwaway checkout of origin/master. It can check the files on disk or, with `--rev`, the commit being pushed. It passes only if both checkers pass, and otherwise prints each FAIL line with its rows. If it breaks (bad file, missing base, a checker crashing) it refuses the push. The one exception is when `check_coverage` can't reach GitHub: it lets the push through, as that checker already does, and prints a line saying the check didn't run.
- **`board.sh`** installs the gate as a pre-push hook in `.boardtree` and in the board job's own checkout. It creates `.boardtree` if it's missing.
  - The hook only checks pushes to `refs/heads/board`, and it judges the commit being pushed.
  - It refuses a push that deletes `board`, and refuses if the gate script is missing.
  - It is set per checkout, so none of your other checkouts of the repo get it.
  - After every tick, `board.sh` re-checks `origin/board`. If it's red, it writes one `BOARD RED` line naming the rows to `logs/board/tick.log`.
- **`roles/board.md`** tells the session what to do when a push is refused: fix the named rows, re-run the gate, and push once it passes. It must never skip the gate or retry the same push unchanged.
- **The selftest** (`selftest.d/97-board-push-gate.sh`) adds 25 checks, each asserting on the output text as well as the exit code. They include a real `git push` to a local bare repo: a red push to `board` is refused, pushes to other branches go through, and a push goes through once the rows are fixed.

**Replaying the real bad commits from 2026-09-26** (read-only, nothing pushed):

| board commit | gate result | rows named |
|---|---|---|
| `ec8ce1a6dc` | refused | 4 blockers naming retired lanes (#272 #275 #281 #382) |
| `3d5b685410` | refused | `done` on open #223 #262 #266 |
| `60c5bd4d80` | refused | `done` on open #31 #223 #262 #266 #287 |
| current `origin/board` (`8f33080740`) | passes | none |

`check_coverage` compares against live GitHub and stops at its first failing check. A later replay of `60c5bd4d80` was still refused, but it named #184 and #315 (closed on GitHub since then) instead of the `done` rows. `NOTES.md` explains this.

**Still open:** the board session can bypass the hook with `git push --no-verify` or by overriding `core.hooksPath`, because `allowed-tools.job` allows every git command. That file belongs to lane.toolsmith, so I sent them the fix on #94 with `deliver.sh`. Until it lands, the post-tick `BOARD RED` line catches a bypass after it happens, but nothing prevents it.
